text:
Maya K: Quick debrief — ran geo failover SLA sims across 3 regions (us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast) using both replay harness and synthetic steady-state traffic. Posting initial findings and a couple of questions.

Tom R: Nice, can you call out which model variants + kernel packs were used? kernel selection often explains weird tail spikes.

Maya K: Sure — main profile used rwd-v2-3b/float16 with kernel-pack v1.9 on west & eu, v2.0 on apac (we wanted to test kernel mismatch fallback). Also ran a quantized run (int8) for one slot to see throughput delta.

Priya S: Observed KV cache thrash when we drained eu region in the replay run. Session affinity drop + switch to fallback model caused repeated cache misses and a ~2.1x token compute increase for a subset of requests.

Alex H: That aligns with the profiler: when routing jumps regions, kernel selection sometimes reinitializes the KV layout and we lose prefix cache. We saw a spike in memcpy and kernel-launch latency in the traces.

Jenna L: Methodology note: we did apples-to-apples by locking concurrency, prompt distribution, and temperature seeds. Replay harness was the recorded production traces from last month; synthetic was poisson arrivals tuned to same qps. Replay surfaced more cache warmup issues.

Maya K: Perf numbers snapshot: steady-state p95 latency: 120ms (west), 140ms (eu), 190ms (apac). During a simulated eu drain -> failover to west, p95 jumped to 420ms for ~45s. Token/sec dropped ~35% during migration window. Quantized slot had better throughput but worse tail.

Tom R: Do we have perf-bot summary links? I want the kernel-level flame charts and the batching stats.

perf-bot: Summary uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1758239999/geo-failover-summary.html — includes flame charts, kernel selection timeline, and batching distribution histograms.

Priya S: Key repro snippet for the replay run (used by replay-harness):
```
replay-run --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-02/slotA --concurrency 40 --pin-model rwd-v2-3b --region-drain eu-central --fallback west
```
We toggled `--force-kernel-v1` to emulate older kernels too.

Alex H: On batching heuristics — the failover path reduced effective batch pooling because requests were split across regions during inflight routing changes. Batcher timeout policy of 8ms failed to gather ideal batches; bumping to 12ms recovered some efficiency but increased avg latency. We should test adaptive timeouts.

Jenna L: Agreed. For apples-to-apples we also normalized token distribution: same prompt lengths and role tokens. Synthetic tests exaggerate concurrency but hide cold-cache effects which replay exposes.

Maya K: Actionable items I propose: 1) Add a KV cache pre-warm when routing target changes for same session id; 2) Add kernel-selection hysteresis so we avoid re-selecting kernels for transient route swaps; 3) Run a second round of sims with adaptive batching (8/10/12ms) and kernel hysteresis flag on.

Tom R: +1 on hysteresis. Add an experiment toggling `kernel_hysteresis_ms=200` vs 1000 to measure stability. Also capture `cudaMemcpy` and `kernel_launch_us` histograms per-region.

Priya S: For the pre-warm: we can piggyback a short KV fetch on the first routed request to warm KV pages, but need to measure cost. Could be a small percent overhead vs big benefit during drain.

infra-bot: Canary policy note — when failing over we allow 2s of connection re-establishment window; recommend increasing to 5s in sim-only mode to replicate network flakiness.

Maya K: I'll run the hysteresis+adaptive-batching sims tomorrow and include kernel pack parity runs (v1.9 vs v2.0 parity) to check cross-kernel behavior. I'll paste results here and link perf-bot artifacts. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Tom R: Thanks — please include the exact commands and seed files so platform can reproduce on Dedicated clusters.

Jenna L: Also, capture per-route cost delta — fallback to west increased token cost by ~18% in these sims; we should quantify at different traffic mixes.

Maya K: Noted. I'll add cost columns and a short write-up on methodology so it's clear how we did apples-to-apples comparisons. End result will be a one-page runbook for running geo failover SLA sims.

perf-bot: Created run artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1758239999/{raw-traces,profiles,summary}.tar.gz

Priya S: One last ask — include a small reproducible test that triggers KV thrash in a matter of seconds so eng-sre can validate mitigations quickly.

Maya K: Will do. Planning to run canary tomorrow at 10:00 PT. I'll notify #eng-oncall before starting.

Tom R: Great. cc @Jenna L for evals to keep an eye on quality regressions during kernel changes.

Jenna L: On it. I'll prepare eval prompts to detect hallucination regressions if we swap quantized models on failover.

Maya K: Thanks team — closing the loop after tomorrow's runs.
